why: Both moved the same single call identically and reached the same core conclusions (cheap default over gpt-5.5-at-high, cacheable prefix, surface failures, catalog-driven vision, client reuse, keep Flex unpinned with measurements), but A shipped more of it as validated branches (prompt budget and a Switchyard offering that B only proposed), backed it with far more live evidence (34 validated calls, multi-arm cost/latency and cache arms), caught the Dockerfile that would have silently left a built image unrouted, and wrote the only honest field-by-field ledger of what the Responses translation keeps, drops and refuses. B's edge is at the rework tier — the native Responses port tying fallback_timeout to the Flex-stall risk, and the BYOK-403 reasoning on which hosts to unlock — plus two sharper correctness catches, which is real but mostly unbuilt.
A_best: m3: a measured, field-by-field account of what the Router path translates, passes through, silently drops (top_k) and refuses outright (seed, logprobs, n>1, non-function tools) — the behaviour-preservation evidence a CTO actually needs — paired with m5, the Dockerfile COPY that would have made a deployed image route nothing with no log line to explain it.
B_best: i7: the native /v1/responses port, argued precisely for the levers policy cannot reach per request — fallback_timeout as the guard against exactly the Flex stall B measured for, per-conversation cache keys, cross-vendor web_search to replace the untranslatable openrouter:web_search entry — with an honest account of the dual-path streaming rewrite it costs.
A_worst: i8 stops at the gpt-6-luna/gpt-4 fixes and reports the Ollama models "unchanged", leaving the substring bug B found (every ollama/* model matched "llama" and got image parts it cannot read); A also never flags that a candidate list and tier selection interact, and claims no change in price from i4 while the fallback list can shift which tier serves.
B_worst: The whole-prompt budget is left as proposal i10 and partly misdiagnosed — caching does not make a 600k-token request fit a 128k context, so "less urgent once i2 lands" is wrong — and the test counts cited in several items (12, 14, 9 assertions) do not appear in the validated test run, which still reports 2 passed.
